query: Marvell electro-optics PAM4 DSP data center demand
normalized: center data demand dsp electro marvell optics pam4

output.content:
**Bottom line:** Marvell’s electro-optics franchise—especially PAM4 optical DSPs, TIAs and laser drivers—is a direct beneficiary of hyperscalers’ AI-cluster buildout, because those clusters require sharply more high-speed optical links both within data centers and across campuses. [[1]]

**What the products do:** Marvell’s PAM4 DSPs target optical links inside cloud and AI data centers at distances of roughly up to 500 meters, supporting 400G, 800G and 1.6T pluggable modules; its coherent DSPs address longer data-center-interconnect links. [[2]] The DSP performs signal-processing functions including equalization, clock and carrier recovery, forward-error correction and coded modulation, while companion TIAs and drivers amplify and condition optical signals. [[1]]

**Demand evidence:** In FY2026, ended January 31, 2026, Marvell generated $6.10 billion of data-center revenue, equal to 74% of total revenue, versus $4.16 billion in FY2025; management attributed the 46% data-center increase to AI-related demand for both custom products and its electro-optics portfolio. [[1]] In the most recently reported quarter, Q2 FY2027 ended August 1, 2026, data-center revenue rose 46% year over year and 18% sequentially to $2.17 billion, representing 79% of company revenue. [[3]] Management characterized AI-related bookings as “exceptionally robust” and cited broad-based connectivity demand, alongside accelerating custom-silicon demand, in raising its outlook. [[3]]

**Technology/ramp read-through:** The immediate volume driver remains 800G, while 1.6T is the next upgrade cycle; Marvell’s Ara platform is a 3nm 1.6T PAM4 optical-interconnect platform with 200G electrical and optical interfaces for AI scale-out. [[4]] [[5]] Marvell has also demonstrated 400G-per-lane PAM4 technology, which it positions as an enabling step toward 3.2T optical interconnects and 204.8T switches. [[5]] The company’s Q1 FY2027 outlook specifically identified demand for 800G and 1.6T scale-out optics, optical scale-up solutions for NPO/CPO, and data-center-interconnect modules. [[6]]

**Why the opportunity can persist:** Marvell’s October 2026 Investor Day estimated the interconnect TAM would grow about 65% annually to approximately $65 billion by 2030, driven by continuing scale-out plus emerging scale-up and scale-across networking. [[7]] Its internal long-range framework therefore depends not merely on server deployment, but on rising optical/electrical connectivity content per AI system as bandwidth, power and latency requirements become more demanding. [[8]]

**Investment implication:** Electro-optics is one of Marvell’s most tangible AI revenue engines today, rather than only a distant option, as FY2026’s reported data-center growth explicitly included the portfolio and Q2 FY2027 data-center revenue maintained 46% year-over-year growth. [[1]] [[3]] The key monitorables are 1.6T adoption and supply availability, the durability of hyperscaler AI capex, Marvell’s ability to preserve its optical-DSP position through the 3.2T transition, and whether scale-up optical architectures such as CPO/LPO move from development into broad deployment. [[5]] [[6]] [[1]]
